```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.4, dpi = 110,
  warning = FALSE, message = FALSE
)
library(rcef)
have_maps <- requireNamespace("maps", quietly = TRUE)
```

# The plots

`rcef` has three families of exploratory plot, all taking **raw CEF
catch** (and a **distributions** table where length / age is involved)
and doing the strata building internally:

* **coverage** - `plot_coverage_heat()` / `_bubble()` / `_bar()` /
  `_map()`: which strata are sampled well enough.
* **discard rate** - `plot_discard_rate()`: the raw per-stratum discard
  rate.
* **length / age distribution** - `plot_numbers_at_length_age()` and
  `plot_meanweight_at_length_age()`: numbers and mean weight at length
  or age.

Every one is a single function that draws with either engine
(`engine = "ggplot"`, the default, or `"base"`), and every one ends its
signature with `palette` then `engine`.

# What the coverage plots answer

One question, four pictures: **for a set of strata, which ones are
sampled well enough, and which are blind spots?** "Sampled well enough"
means different things depending on what you are about to estimate, so
`what` switches it:

* `what = "discard"` (the default) - does the stratum have a discard
  estimate at all, and from enough trips?
* `what = "length"` - is there a length distribution linked to this
  stratum's catch, from enough measured fish?
* `what = "age"` - the same, for an age distribution.

Every function here takes **raw CEF catch** (and, for `"length"` /
`"age"`, a **distributions** table) and builds and classifies the strata
internally. There is nothing to pre-compute: no `build_strata()`, no
`classify_strata()` call of your own.

```{r data}
data(anchoveta_catch)   # ~3,500 rows of dummy Southeast-Pacific anchoveta CEF catch
data(anchoveta_dist)    # its length + age distributions

dim(anchoveta_catch)
table(anchoveta_catch$catchCategory)
table(anchoveta_catch$Country)
table(anchoveta_dist$distributionType)
```

`anchoveta_catch` is a fully invented data set - nothing in it is copied
from a real stock - covering seven flag states over FAO Area 87
(Pacific, Southeast), four years and four quarters. It is already
through `derive_fields()`, so the grouping columns the plots use
(`Country`, `Season`, `metier4`, ...) are present. Coverage is
deliberately uneven: Peru and Chile land the most and sample best, the
distant-water fleets least.

## The four views

| Function                 | Picture                                   | Best for |
|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------|----------|
| `plot_coverage_heat()`   | a status colour per `y` x `x` cell        | spotting blind spots across two categories at a glance |
| `plot_coverage_bubble()` | the same grid, bubble area = weight       | when the *size* of the gap matters, not just its presence |
| `plot_coverage_bar()`    | sampled vs un-sampled weight, per `y`     | "how much of the catch is behind the estimate?" |
| `plot_coverage_map()`    | one sampled/not pie per area              | where, geographically, the gaps are |

`y` is the only required grouping argument. `heat` / `bubble` put a
second category on `x`; `bar` puts it on `fill`.

# Discard coverage

## Start simple: one category

```{r disc-heat-1, fig.alt = "Coverage heatmap of discard sampling status by metier"}
plot_coverage_heat(anchoveta_catch, y = "metier4")
```

Each row is a metier; the single column collapses everything else. The
cell colour is the stratum's classified status (see
[Reading the status scale](#reading-the-status-scale)).

## Add a second category and facets

```{r disc-heat-2, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Coverage heatmap by metier and fleet region, faceted by season"}
plot_coverage_heat(anchoveta_catch,
                   y = "metier4", x = "Country", facet = "Season")
```

`y`, `x` and `facet` are the strata: the classification is done at that
resolution. Change them and the picture, and the underlying pass/fail,
changes with it.

## The thresholds: `min_cov` and `min_trip`

`min_cov` is the minimum share of the weight that must be covered
(percent, 0-100); `min_trip` the minimum number of sampling trips. They
sit next to each other in every signature, together with `min_fish`
(measurements, used only for `"length"` / `"age"`):

```{r disc-heat-thr, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "The same heatmap with a stricter coverage threshold"}
plot_coverage_heat(anchoveta_catch,
                   y = "metier4", x = "Country", facet = "Season",
                   min_cov = 80, min_trip = 3)
```

Raising `min_cov` from its default 50 to 80 demotes every stratum that
was scraping by. A bar chart shows sampled-vs-unsampled *weight*, which
neither threshold changes - passing `min_cov` or `min_trip` to
`plot_coverage_bar()` is therefore an error, not a silent no-op.

## Bubbles: weight the gaps

```{r disc-bubble, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Coverage bubble grid, bubble area proportional to landed weight"}
plot_coverage_bubble(anchoveta_catch,
                     y = "metier4", x = "Country", min_cov = 50, min_trip = 2)
```

Same grid as the heatmap, but a tiny un-sampled stratum now reads as a
tiny bubble - you can tell "small problem" from "the bulk of the
fishery is blind".

## Bars: how much weight is behind the estimate

```{r disc-bar, fig.alt = "Sampled versus unsampled weight per metier, filled by fleet region"}
plot_coverage_bar(anchoveta_catch, y = "metier4", fill = "Country")
```

```{r disc-bar-facet, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "The same bar chart, one panel per season"}
plot_coverage_bar(anchoveta_catch, y = "metier4", fill = "Country",
                  facet = "Season")
```

## Map: where the gaps are

```{r disc-map, eval = have_maps, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Coverage map, one sampled/not-sampled pie per FAO Area 87 division"}
plot_coverage_map(anchoveta_catch, engine = "ggplot")
```

```{r disc-map-grouped, eval = have_maps, fig.height = 5.5, fig.alt = "Coverage map with one boxed grid of pies per area, split by quarter"}
plot_coverage_map(anchoveta_catch, group = "Season", engine = "ggplot")
```

(The map needs the suggested `maps` package. It resolves the FAO Area 87
divisions to centroids off the Peru and Chile coasts. `group` gives one
labelled box of pies per area, one pie per level.)

# Length coverage

Pass `distributions` and `what = "length"`. `catchCategory` picks which
catch part the distribution is judged against and appears in the plot
title: it defaults to **`"All"`** (landings and discards together,
titled "catch") and also takes `"Lan"`, `"Dis"` or `"BMS"`. `min_fish`
is the minimum number of measured fish for a stratum to count as
covered.

```{r len-catch, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Length-sampling coverage of the whole catch, by metier and fleet region"}
plot_coverage_heat(anchoveta_catch, y = "metier4", x = "Country",
                   what = "length", distributions = anchoveta_dist,
                   min_cov = 50, min_fish = 25, min_trip = 2)   # catchCategory = "All"
```

```{r len-lan, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Length-sampling coverage of the landings"}
plot_coverage_heat(anchoveta_catch, y = "metier4", x = "Country",
                   what = "length", catchCategory = "Lan",
                   distributions = anchoveta_dist,
                   min_cov = 50, min_fish = 25, min_trip = 2)
```

```{r len-dis, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Length-sampling coverage of the discards"}
plot_coverage_heat(anchoveta_catch, y = "metier4", x = "Country",
                   what = "length", catchCategory = "Dis",
                   distributions = anchoveta_dist,
                   min_cov = 50, min_fish = 25, min_trip = 2)
```

The title carries the catch part - "Length sampling coverage vs
threshold (catch)" / "(landings)" / "(discards)". It is derived from
`what` and `catchCategory`; there is no `weight_label` argument to set.

The bar and bubble views take exactly the same arguments:

```{r len-bar, fig.alt = "Length-sampled versus unsampled landed weight per metier"}
plot_coverage_bar(anchoveta_catch, y = "metier4", fill = "Country",
                  what = "length", distributions = anchoveta_dist)
```

# Age coverage

Identical call, `what = "age"` (`anchoveta_dist` carries `Age` rows,
ages 0-7). `catchCategory` again defaults to `"All"` and titles the
figure "(catch)".

Where a `metier4` x `Country` cell is blank, that fleet never worked
that metier - a genuine hole, not an unsampled stratum. A stratum that
operated but landed nothing shows in the near-white "no landings /
no discards" colour.

```{r age-heat, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Age-sampling coverage of the catch, by metier and fleet region"}
plot_coverage_heat(anchoveta_catch, y = "metier4", x = "Country",
                   what = "age", distributions = anchoveta_dist,
                   min_cov = 50, min_fish = 15, min_trip = 2)
```

```{r age-dis, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Age-sampling coverage of the discards"}
plot_coverage_heat(anchoveta_catch, y = "metier4", x = "Country",
                   what = "age", catchCategory = "Dis",
                   distributions = anchoveta_dist,
                   min_cov = 50, min_fish = 15, min_trip = 2)
```

```{r age-bubble, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Age-sampling coverage as a weighted bubble grid"}
plot_coverage_bubble(anchoveta_catch, y = "metier4", x = "Country",
                     what = "age", distributions = anchoveta_dist,
                     min_cov = 50, min_fish = 15, min_trip = 2)
```

# Reading the status scale

The heatmap and bubble colours are a fixed semantic scale (green = safe,
amber = warning, grey = nothing to sample), so asking for
`palette = "colorblind"` there does nothing and warns. `palette` *does*
recolour the bar chart's fill.

The status legend always lists **every** category with its colour, even
the ones no cell in the current figure lands in - so the same figure
drawn on two different subsets has the same key, and an absent category
reads as "nothing here", not "not a category".

# Discard rate

`plot_discard_rate()` draws one point per stratum: its discard rate,
`discards / (landings + discards)`. A stratum here is one
`x` + `colour` + `shape` + `facet` cell - each point is that cell's own
discards over its own landings plus discards, straight from
`build_strata()`. It is **not** an average of anything finer: change
`x` (or `colour` / `shape` / `facet`) and the strata, and the points,
are rebuilt at that resolution. `x` is required; everything else is
optional.

```{r dr-basic, fig.alt = "Discard rate per stratum, by metier"}
plot_discard_rate(anchoveta_catch, x = "metier4")
```

Map a column to `colour` (point fill) and another to `shape`:

```{r dr-colour-shape, fig.height = 4.6, fig.alt = "Discard rate by metier, coloured by country and shaped by quarter"}
plot_discard_rate(anchoveta_catch, x = "metier4",
                  colour = "Country", shape = "Season")
```

`facet` splits the panel; `jitter = FALSE` stops the horizontal spread
(useful when there are few strata per `x`):

```{r dr-facet, fig.height = 5.5, fig.alt = "Discard rate by metier, coloured by country, one panel per quarter"}
plot_discard_rate(anchoveta_catch, x = "Country", colour = "metier4",
                  facet = "Season", jitter = FALSE)
```

The base engine draws the same figure without ggplot2 on the call path:

```{r dr-base, fig.alt = "Discard rate per stratum, base-graphics engine"}
plot_discard_rate(anchoveta_catch, x = "metier4", colour = "Country",
                  engine = "base")
```

# Numbers at length and age

`plot_numbers_at_length_age()` takes raw catch + `distributions`, links
them and sums the numbers at each class, drawn as a histogram.
`distributionType` picks `"LengthTotal"` (default) or `"Age"`.
`catchCategory` picks the catch part and titles the plot: it defaults
to **`"All"`** - landings and discards together, titled "catch" - and
also takes `"Lan"`, `"Dis"` or `"BMS"`.

## Numbers at length

```{r num-len-catch, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Numbers at length, landings and discards combined, by country"}
plot_numbers_at_length_age(anchoveta_catch, anchoveta_dist,
                           fill = "Country")                    # catchCategory = "All"
```

```{r num-len-lan, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Numbers at length of the landings, by country"}
plot_numbers_at_length_age(anchoveta_catch, anchoveta_dist,
                           catchCategory = "Lan", fill = "Country")
```

```{r num-len-dis, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Numbers at length of the discards, by country"}
plot_numbers_at_length_age(anchoveta_catch, anchoveta_dist,
                           catchCategory = "Dis", fill = "Country")
```

`stacked = FALSE` dodges the bars instead of stacking; `facet` takes one
or two columns (`c("row", "col")` becomes a grid) and, with
`scales = "free_y"`, lets each panel set its own range:

```{r num-len-dodge, fig.height = 4.4, fig.alt = "Numbers at length, dodged bars per country"}
plot_numbers_at_length_age(anchoveta_catch, anchoveta_dist,
                           fill = "Country", stacked = FALSE)
```

```{r num-len-facets, fig.height = 6.5, fig.alt = "Numbers at length faceted by quarter and metier"}
plot_numbers_at_length_age(anchoveta_catch, anchoveta_dist,
                           fill = "Country", facet = c("Season", "metier4"),
                           scales = "free_y")
```

## Numbers at age

```{r num-age-catch, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Numbers at age, landings and discards combined, by country"}
plot_numbers_at_length_age(anchoveta_catch, anchoveta_dist,
                           distributionType = "Age", fill = "Country")
```

```{r num-age-lan, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Numbers at age of the landings, by country"}
plot_numbers_at_length_age(anchoveta_catch, anchoveta_dist,
                           distributionType = "Age", catchCategory = "Lan",
                           fill = "Country")
```

```{r num-age-dis, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Numbers at age of the discards, by country"}
plot_numbers_at_length_age(anchoveta_catch, anchoveta_dist,
                           distributionType = "Age", catchCategory = "Dis",
                           fill = "Country")
```

```{r num-age-base, fig.height = 4.4, fig.alt = "Numbers at age histogram, base engine, one panel per quarter"}
plot_numbers_at_length_age(anchoveta_catch, anchoveta_dist,
                           distributionType = "Age", fill = "Country",
                           facet = "Season", engine = "base", n_per_screen = 2)
```

# Mean weight at length and age

`plot_meanweight_at_length_age()` draws mean weight at class as a line
with points, plus a +/- 1 sd band when the strata are averaged (no
`shape`). `colour` groups the lines; `catchCategory` works exactly as
above and defaults to `"All"` ("catch").

## Mean weight at length

```{r mw-len-catch, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Mean weight at length, landings and discards combined"}
plot_meanweight_at_length_age(anchoveta_catch, anchoveta_dist,
                              colour = "Country")                # catchCategory = "All"
```

```{r mw-len-lan, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Mean weight at length of the landings"}
plot_meanweight_at_length_age(anchoveta_catch, anchoveta_dist,
                              catchCategory = "Lan", colour = "Country")
```

```{r mw-len-dis, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Mean weight at length of the discards"}
plot_meanweight_at_length_age(anchoveta_catch, anchoveta_dist,
                              catchCategory = "Dis", colour = "Country")
```

`shape` opens the averaged group back up (one series per level) and
drops the band; `facet` splits into panels; the base engine draws the
same figure:

```{r mw-len-shape, fig.height = 4.4, fig.alt = "Mean weight at length, separate series per quarter"}
plot_meanweight_at_length_age(anchoveta_catch, anchoveta_dist,
                              shape = "Season")
```

```{r mw-len-facet-base, fig.height = 5.5, fig.alt = "Mean weight at length faceted by quarter, base engine"}
plot_meanweight_at_length_age(anchoveta_catch, anchoveta_dist,
                              colour = "Country", facet = "Season",
                              engine = "base")
```

## Mean weight at age

```{r mw-age-catch, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Mean weight at age, landings and discards combined"}
plot_meanweight_at_length_age(anchoveta_catch, anchoveta_dist,
                              distributionType = "Age", colour = "Country")
```

```{r mw-age-lan, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Mean weight at age of the landings"}
plot_meanweight_at_length_age(anchoveta_catch, anchoveta_dist,
                              distributionType = "Age", catchCategory = "Lan",
                              colour = "Country")
```

```{r mw-age-dis, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Mean weight at age of the discards"}
plot_meanweight_at_length_age(anchoveta_catch, anchoveta_dist,
                              distributionType = "Age", catchCategory = "Dis",
                              colour = "Country")
```

# Base R vs ggplot2 on a heavier table

Every function draws with either engine from the one call:
`engine = "ggplot"` (default) returns a ggplot object; `engine = "base"`
draws straight to the current device with base graphics and returns
`NULL`. The base engine has no ggplot2 or grid on the call path, which
can matter when a figure is redrawn on every input change in an app.

```{r timing, echo = TRUE}
bench <- function(expr) {
  expr <- substitute(expr)
  grDevices::pdf(NULL); on.exit(grDevices::dev.off())
  min(replicate(5, system.time(eval(expr, parent.frame()))[["elapsed"]]))
}

gg   <- bench(plot_coverage_heat(anchoveta_catch, y = "metier4",
                                 x = "Country", facet = "Season"))
base <- bench(plot_coverage_heat(anchoveta_catch, y = "metier4",
                                 x = "Country", facet = "Season",
                                 engine = "base"))
data.frame(engine = c("ggplot", "base"),
           seconds = round(c(gg, base), 3),
           row.names = NULL)
```

```{r timing-len, echo = TRUE}
gg_l   <- bench(plot_coverage_heat(anchoveta_catch, y = "metier4", x = "Country",
                                   what = "length", distributions = anchoveta_dist,
                                   min_fish = 25))
base_l <- bench(plot_coverage_heat(anchoveta_catch, y = "metier4", x = "Country",
                                   what = "length", distributions = anchoveta_dist,
                                   min_fish = 25, engine = "base"))
data.frame(engine = c("ggplot", "base"),
           seconds = round(c(gg_l, base_l), 3),
           row.names = NULL)
```

For a static figure the difference is usually small - most of the time
for a `"length"` / `"age"` figure is the link-and-classify step, which
both engines share. The base engine's advantage shows up under repeated
redraws, not in a single call.

# Argument reference

Shared across `plot_coverage_heat()` / `_bubble()` / `_bar()` /
`_map()`:

The arguments are ordered the way you build a call: **what data**, then
**which columns**, then **thresholds**, then **rendering**, and
`palette` then `engine` last.

| Group | Argument | Meaning |
|-------|----------|---------|
| data      | `catch`          | raw CEF catch (already `derive_fields()`-ed) |
| data      | `distributions`  | CEF distributions table; required for `what = "length"` / `"age"` |
| data      | `what`           | `"discard"` (default), `"length"`, `"age"` |
| data      | `catchCategory`  | `"All"` (default - landings + discards, titled "catch") / `"Lan"` / `"Dis"` / `"BMS"` for `"length"` / `"age"`; invalid for `"discard"` |
| columns   | `y`              | row category (required) |
| columns   | `x` / `fill`     | second category - `x` for heat/bubble, `fill` for bar |
| columns   | `facet`          | optional facet column |
| threshold | `min_cov`        | minimum coverage, percent (heat / bubble) |
| threshold | `min_trip`       | minimum sampling trips (heat / bubble) |
| threshold | `min_fish`       | minimum measured fish (`"length"` / `"age"`) |
| render    | `n_per_screen`   | base engine: split a faceted figure across devices |
| last      | `palette`        | `"default"` or `"colorblind"` (bar fill only) |
| last      | `engine`         | `"ggplot"` (default) or `"base"` |

There is deliberately **no** `dims`, `weight_label`, `angle` or
`show_fill_in_labels` argument: the strata come from
`y` / `x` / `fill` / `facet`, the weight word from `what` /
`catchCategory`, and the x-label rotation is fixed.

`plot_discard_rate()` adds:

| Argument | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `x`      | x-axis category (required); strata built on `x` + `colour` + `shape` + `facet` |
| `colour` | column mapped to point fill |
| `shape`  | column mapped to point shape |
| `facet`  | optional facet column |
| `jitter` | jitter the points horizontally (default `TRUE`) |

`plot_numbers_at_length_age()` / `plot_meanweight_at_length_age()` add:

| Argument | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `distributions`   | CEF distributions table (linked to `data` internally) |
| `distributionType`| `"LengthTotal"` (default) or `"Age"` |
| `catchCategory`   | `"All"` (default) / `"Lan"` / `"Dis"` / `"BMS"`; feeds the title |
| `fill` / `colour` | grouping column (`fill` for numbers, `colour` for mean weight) |
| `facet`           | one or two facet columns (`c("row", "col")` becomes a grid) |
| `stacked`         | numbers histogram: stack (default) or dodge on `fill` |
| `shape`           | mean weight: separate series per level, drops the sd band |
| `scales`          | ggplot facet scales: `"fixed"` (default), `"free_x"`, `"free_y"`, `"free"` |
